_why: Which parts of the canonical replay document BOTH sides can produce today.
The differential layer lands module by module: curve_ref.py mirrors auction.rs, settle_ref.py
mirrors settle.rs and finalize_round, claims_ref.py mirrors claims.rs and claim_withdraw. The
Python side has all three; the Rust side has whichever replays exist.
Entries are PATHS, not whole sections, and that granularity is load-bearing rather than
fussy. claims_ref returns per_bidder AND withdraw_claims: the first is claim_payout and
claim_refund, which are DEV3's and exist; the second is claim_withdraw, which is DEV1's, and
it needs pps from a settle replay that does not exist yet. Declaring the whole section would
claim coverage of a half nobody has replayed - the silent-subset defect this file exists to
Self-checking in both directions: run_vectors.py --out emits exactly these paths, and
test_vectors.rs asserts that what it emits is exactly these paths. Adding a Rust replay
without widening this list fails the Rust test; widening it without the replay fails the diff.
To widen: add the path here in the same commit as the Rust replay that produces it.

_read_this_before_changing_either_side: Building the generated corpus (ANTARES_VECTOR_DUMP) currently makes the diff fail on about
87 of 204 vectors, from ONE root cause, and it is a specification question rather than a bug
in either implementation. Do not 'fix' curve_ref.py and do not 'fix' auction.rs.
SYMPTOM: after a full subscription, curve_ref.py reports SoldOut for the next bid (or keeps
evaluating the curve and reports PremiumAboveMax), while auction.rs reports WrongPhase.
WHY auction.rs IS RIGHT. 02-CONTRACT-SPEC §5 step 6 sets phase = Active *immediately* on full
subscription, and §16's canonical bid order checks phase/time BEFORE filled is computed. So a
post-sellout bid meets the phase check first. DEV-PROTOCOL §1's corollary makes
02-CONTRACT-SPEC authoritative for contract behaviour.
THE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL FINDING: SoldOut (error 33) is unreachable through the
contract's own paths. filled = min(notional, remaining) with notional > 0 already checked, so
filled == 0 iff remaining == 0 iff notional_sold == notional_offered - and step 6 flips the
phase the instant that holds, while the phase check runs first. open_epoch sets
notional_sold = 0 and requires locked_assets >= min_fill > 0, so notional_offered > 0. There
is therefore no reachable state with phase == Auction and filled == 0.
That is the same shape as codes 5 / 23 / 28 / 55 / 56, which D-60 retired as 'ABI an
integrator must handle and can never observe'.
AND 06-TEST-PLAN §5's OWN SCHEMA NOTE IS THE CONTRADICTING TEXT: it lists SoldOut among the
diffable curve-arithmetic rejects and scopes WrongPhase to 'a bid at or past
open.at + auction_duration', i.e. time only. One of those two documents has to move.
OWNERS: 02-CONTRACT-SPEC §3/§16 is DEV1's; 06-TEST-PLAN §5 is shared. Raised by DEV3 in
plan/STANDUP.md. Until it is ruled, the four hand-written vectors are green and a corpus build
is red for this reason and no other - verified by categorising every field-level difference.
